defects.title: Migration rollout is not covered against populated data
defects.body: Premise: `0006` mutates populated `admin_users` rows at lines 26–31, but the repository has no test that runs the migration against the preceding schema and a legacy user/application decision. → Path: a future edit to the ordering, backfill, or constraints can pass the fake-DB action suite without exercising the deployed DDL path. → Verdict: the required populated-database compatibility behavior can regress undetected.
evidence: Premise: `0006` changes populated `admin_users` rows → Path: no automated migration invocation establishes the pre-0006 legacy-user/decision state → Verdict: rollout compatibility regressions are not detected before deployment.
drizzle/0006_flimsy_spacker_dave.sql:26-31 → role is added nullable, backfilled, constrained, then made non-null on an existing table.

.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/task_01.md:105-111 → the implementation contract explicitly requires integration coverage for legacy identities, decision references, constraints, foreign keys, and additive migration behavior.
rg -n -i 'migration|migrat|0006|legacy' __tests__ → no test file invokes Drizzle migrations or creates the required pre-0006 populated database state.

suppressions.candidate: Role constraints could reject legacy accounts during rollout
suppressions.note: The migration explicitly adds nullable role, backfills every null role to admin, then adds the check and non-null enforcement; this matches the documented migration sequence.

suppressions.candidate: New foreign keys could invalidate the existing data model
suppressions.note: Both new tables start empty and their foreign keys target pre-existing primary keys; the specified application cascade and staff restriction are encoded explicitly.
